card.name: Advice on who should not use a product
card.fires_on: Words right after a condition that rules someone out, such as 'patients who cannot follow this advice should not take' or 'if you are unsure, do not attempt'. It fires on the verb or auxiliary that finishes the instruction.

modes.label: Cannot comply, should not take
modes.description: Verb or auxiliary after a clause about patients unable to follow instructions.
modes.example: Patients who cannot follow this advice should not<< take>> REYVOW. Prescribers

modes.label: If unsure, do not attempt
modes.description: The comma or 'not' after an if-unsure clause that tells the reader to stop.
modes.example: If you are unsure of the necessary steps to safely insert and/or remove NEXPLANON, do<< not>> attempt the procedure.

modes.label: Alternative product should be used
modes.description: Auxiliary 'should' or 'be' pointing to the suitable option when another is not fit.
modes.example: If less than 0.3 mL is needed the ZARXIO single-dose vial<< should>> be used.

card.writes: It pushes toward words meaning not suitable, quit or not advisable, especially Chinese terms and 'quit'.
card.plain: It lights up where the label says who should not use the drug or should stop and not go ahead.
